issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator appointed by a court cannot award relief beyond the claim specified in the court’s reference without a further order of reference.
material_facts: The claimant’s application and plaint sought Rs. 68,582 for additional transport costs and Rs. 25,000 for road construction, for a total claim of Rs. 93,582.
The court referred the matters claimed in the plaint to the arbitrator.
Before the arbitrator, the claimant advanced an additional Rs. 68,582 for transport, beyond the transport claim specified in the plaint and reference.
The arbitrator rejected the road-construction claim but awarded Rs. 1,16,570 for transport.
issues.conclusion: The arbitrator exceeded the scope of the reference by allowing the additional transport claim. The award could not exceed the specified transport claim of Rs. 68,582.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 20(1) and 20(4) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, when an agreement is filed in court and the court makes an order of reference, the arbitrator’s authority is limited to the relief referred. If the claim is specified in the plaint and the reference is confined to that claim, the arbitrator cannot enlarge the reference or entertain a fresh claim without a further court order. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.court_referred_arbitration: The dispute was referred to an arbitrator by a court order.
predicates.claim_amount_specified: The claimant specified a monetary limit for the claim in the pleading incorporated into the reference.
predicates.additional_claim_outside_reference: The claimant advanced before the arbitrator an additional claim that was not included in the specified claim referred by the court.

issues.definition: When a court refers a dispute with a specified claim and the claimant advances an additional claim outside that reference, the arbitrator must confine the award to the referred claim.

issues.legal_issue: An award may be confirmed to the extent it falls within the referred claim when the appellant does not object to that portion.
material_facts: The arbitrator awarded Rs. 1,16,570 for transport, although the transport claim specified in the plaint and reference was Rs. 68,582.
The appellant had no objection to the award being accepted to the extent of Rs. 68,582.
The Court confirmed that portion with interest from the date of the award.
issues.conclusion: The award was confirmed to the extent of Rs. 68,582, together with interest at six per cent per annum from the date of the award.
issues.legal_principle: The Court limited the award to the amount within the reference and, as the appellant did not object to accepting that portion, confirmed it with the interest specified in the award. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.court_referred_arbitration: The dispute was referred to an arbitrator by a court order.
predicates.award_includes_amount_within_reference: The arbitrator’s award includes an amount that falls within the claim referred by the court.
predicates.appellant_does_not_object_to_that_amount: The appellant does not object to confirmation of the portion of the award that falls within the referred claim.

issues.definition: When a court-referred arbitration award includes an amount within the reference and the appellant does not object to that amount, that portion of the award is confirmed.

issues.legal_issue: A direction to return security deposits and earnest money need not be disturbed when the appellant does not dispute the claimant’s entitlement to those amounts.
material_facts: The award directed the appellant to return the claimant’s security deposits and earnest money, with interest from the date of the award.
The appellant did not contend that the claimant was not entitled to those amounts.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not interfere with the direction to return the security deposits and earnest money with interest at six per cent per annum from the date of the award.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to interfere with the payment direction because the appellant did not dispute the claimant’s entitlement to the amounts. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.award_directs_return_of_security_or_earn: The award directs one party to return security deposits or earnest money to the other party.
predicates.appellant_does_not_dispute_entitlement: The appellant does not contend that the recipient is not entitled to the security deposits or earnest money.

issues.definition: When an award directs the return of security deposits or earnest money and the appellant does not dispute the recipient’s entitlement, the return direction is not disturbed.
